summary.title: Logging Cheat Sheet
summary.one_liner: Learn what to log in application security logging (events, attributes, and what to exclude), how to collect and protect logs, and how to verify logging works, following OWASP guidance.
takeaways: Application logs should record when, where, who and what for each security-relevant event, such as authentication successes and failures, authorization failures and input validation failures.
Never log secrets such as passwords, session IDs, access tokens, encryption keys or payment card data; mask, hash or remove them, and only log data that is legally sanctioned.
Sanitize event data to prevent log injection (CR, LF and delimiters), and make sure logging failures do not break the application.
Protect logs with restricted access, separate storage or accounts, tamper detection, read-only media and centralized collection over secure transport.
Verify logging during code review and testing, including injection, resource exhaustion and simulated logging failures.
summary.summary: The OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet gives developers concise guidance on building application logging, focused on security event logging. It explains the operational and security purposes of logs, where event data comes from and where it should be stored, and which events to log, such as authentication, authorization and input validation failures. It also covers the event attributes to record, data that must be excluded or masked, customizable log levels, and how to collect, protect, deploy and verify logging, including a sample network architecture for centralized log collection.
